content: 1. Clarithromycin can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored to mitigate risks. 2. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of trimipramine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is serious and alternative therapies should be considered. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval, so their concurrent use should be avoided or replaced with alternative drugs. 3. Triptorelin increases the toxicity of clarithromycin by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely, as this combination increases the risk of torsades de pointes. 4. Clarithromycin and tropisetron both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 5. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Concomitant use of tucatinib with CYP3A substrates can lead to serious or life-threatening toxicities. If unavoidable, reduce the dose of the CYP3A substrate as per product labeling. 6. Clarithromycin decreases the effects of the live typhoid vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Wait until antibiotic therapy is complete before administering live bacterial vaccines. 7. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of ubrogepant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 8. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of ulipristal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol inhaled by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Vilanterol is a CYP3A4 substrate, and coadministration with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure. 10. Clarithromycin increases the toxicity of umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol inhaled by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Exercise extreme caution when vilanterol is coadministered with drugs that prolong the QTc interval, as adrenergic agonist effects on the cardiovascular system may be potentiated. 11. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of upadacitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Caution is advised if upadacitinib is coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 12. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of valbenazine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Both valbenazine and clarithromycin prolong the QTc interval, so use caution and monitor closely. 13. Clarithromycin increases levels of valproic acid by decreasing its metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 14. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of valsartan by affecting hepatic uptake transporter OATP1B1. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with OATP1B1 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure to valsartan. 15. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of vamorolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Reduce the starting dose of vamorolone to 4 mg/kg/day, not exceeding 200 mg/day if the patient weighs more than 50 kg. 16. Clarithromycin and vandetanib both increase each other’s toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Clarithromycin also increases the levels or effects of vandetanib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. 17. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of vardenafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored, with a maximum dose of 5 mg/24 hours. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, so avoid or use alternative drugs. 18. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of velpatasvir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of vemurafenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, so avoid or use alternative drugs. Concomitant use of vemurafenib with drugs that prolong the QT interval is not recommended. 20. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of venetoclax by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated during the initial ramp-up dosing phase of venetoclax. If a P-gp inhibitor must be used, reduce the venetoclax dose by at least 50% and monitor closely for signs of toxicity. 21. Clarithromycin and venlafaxine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Clarithromycin also increases the levels or effects of venlafaxine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. 22. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of verapamil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely, as increased effects of calcium channel blockers may lead to hypotension, edema, decreased heart rate, and acute kidney injury due to reduced renal blood flow. Verapamil also increases the levels or effects of clarithromycin, but the clinical significance is unknown. 23. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of vilanterol/fluticasone furoate inhaled by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Both fluticasone furoate and vilanterol are CYP3A4 substrates, and coadministration with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure. 24. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of vilazodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If intolerable adverse effects occur with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors, reduce the daily dose of vilazodone to 20 mg. 25. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of vinblastine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of vincristine and vincristine liposomal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of vinorelbine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of voclosporin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely, as both drugs can increase each other’s effects by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution or consider alternative therapies. 29. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of vorapaxar by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 30. Clarithromycin and voriconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Clarithromycin also increases the levels or effects of voriconazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Voriconazole may also increase the levels or effects of clarithromycin, but the clinical significance is unknown. 31. Clarithromycin and vorinostat both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 32. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of voxilaprevir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 33. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of warfarin by affecting its metabolism. Monitor INR more frequently and adjust the warfarin dose as needed. 34. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of zaleplon by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 35. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of zanubrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Reduce the zanubrutinib dose to 80 mg twice daily when coadministered with clarithromycin 250 mg twice daily, or to 80 mg once daily with clarithromycin 500 mg twice daily. Resume the previous zanubrutinib dose after discontinuing clarithromycin. 36. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of zavegepant intranasal by affecting OATP1B3 transporters. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 37. Clarithromycin increases the toxicity of zidovudine by an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Separate administration by at least 2 to 4 hours. 38. Clarithromycin and ziprasidone both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Clarithromycin also increases the levels or effects of ziprasidone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. 39. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of zolpidem by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 40. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of zonisamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of zuranolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Reduce the zuranolone dose if coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 42. Hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, have been reported with clarithromycin, amoxicillin, and vonoprazan. Discontinue immediately if hypersensitivity occurs and initiate appropriate treatment. 43. Severe cutaneous adverse reactions (SCAR), including Stevens-Johnson syndrome (SJS) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN), have been reported with all components. Discontinue at the first signs of SCAR. 44. Clostridioides difficile-associated diarrhea (CDAD) has been reported with acid-suppressing therapies and nearly all antibacterial agents. Discontinue therapy and implement appropriate management if CDAD is confirmed. 45. Avoid amoxicillin in patients with mononucleosis, as a high percentage develop an erythematous skin rash. 46. Use of this regimen without a proven or strongly suspected bacterial infection increases the risk of drug-resistant bacteria. 47. Serum chromogranin A (CgA) levels may increase due to drug-induced decreases in gastric acidity, potentially causing false-positive results in neuroendocrine tumor diagnostics. Assess CgA levels at least 14 days after treatment. 48. High urine concentrations of amoxicillin may cause false-positive glucose test results when using Benedict’s copper reduction tests. Use enzymatic glucose oxidase reactions instead. 49. Vonoprazan is a CYP3A substrate, a weak CYP3A inhibitor, and a CYP2C19 inhibitor. 50. Clarithromycin is a CYP3A substrate and a strong CYP3A inhibitor. 51. Clarithromycin is not recommended during pregnancy unless no alternative therapy is appropriate, as observational studies have shown adverse effects on pregnancy outcomes, including increased risks of miscarriage and fetal malformations. 52. Report pregnancies to Phathom Pharmaceuticals, Inc., via their adverse event reporting line at 1-800-775-PHAT (7428). 53. Store the medication at 20–25°C (68–77°F), with brief exposure to 15–30°C (59–86°F) permitted. Protect from light.
